title: Beams and frames
summary: How supports change the bending moment in a beam, and how a frame sways under a side load.

steps.title: The cantilever
steps.text: A 4 m steel cantilever (an IPE 300 section: I = 8356 cm⁴) carries 10 kN at its tip. Beam theory says the tip deflects δ = P L³ / 3 E I. Run it and compare the Max displacement in the Summary; the Bending moment tab shows the moment growing linearly to P L = 40 kN·m at the wall.

check.success: 12.77 mm, exactly P L³ / 3 E I.

steps.title: Simply supported
steps.text: A 6 m beam on a pin and a roller under 5 kN/m. The moment is a parabola, largest at mid-span: w L² / 8. Run it and read Max |M|.

steps.title: Fix the ends
steps.text: Build the same beam into walls at both ends. The ends now resist rotation, which lifts the whole moment diagram: hogging moments at the walls, a smaller sagging moment in the middle, and the largest moment drops to w L² / 12.

check.success: 15 kN·m at the walls, 7.5 kN·m at mid-span, and a fifth of the deflection.

steps.title: A portal frame sways
steps.text: A frame resists a side load (wind) through the bending of its columns and beam, joined rigidly at the corners. Run the portal frame and look at the Deflected shape: it leans over, and the corners stay square.

check.success: A few millimetres of sway, with moments at the bases and corners.

steps.title: Change the shape
steps.text: On the Model tab, drag a top corner of the portal frame up or sideways (it snaps to 0.5 m), then run again and watch the moment diagram change. Each drag is one step you can undo.

check.success: Taller columns sway more; a sloping beam carries some load by axial force.
